recentItems.title: Iran's Araghchi briefs China ahead of Xi-Trump meeting in Washington
recentItems.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has arrived in Beijing for talks with his Chinese counterpart, as Tehran faces growing military and economic pressure from the United States and sanctions from the UN. The visit comes a week before Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to meet US President Donald Trump in Washington, and is Araghchi's second trip to Beijing since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February. China is Iran's largest economic and trade partner and buys about 90 per cent of Iran's oil exports, while also maintaining strong relations with Saudi Arabia and other regional powers. Beijing is calling for restraint, a return to dialogue and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as the conflict continues to threaten shipping and trade across the region. China has also been hosting a 13-member Taliban delegation at the Xiangshan Defense Forum, despite not formally recognising the Taliban government, reflecting Beijing's policy of engaging with a wide range of countries. Tehran is expected to brief Beijing on its confrontation with Washington, while China continues to support the 2015 nuclear deal and says any future agreement should build on the existing framework. 

Al Jazeera's Katrina Yu reports from Beijing and Sinem Koseoglu from Tehran.

recentItems.title: US holds back from Yemen war as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi pressure: Analysis
recentItems.description:
The Houthis have rejected reports that one of their drones was intercepted heading towards Mecca, calling the claim "a nauseating lie". 
Oil prices have climbed after tanker loading was halted at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu, following an attack on the East-West pipeline that could take five weeks to repair. 
Saudi Arabia and Egypt are calling for free navigation in the Red Sea as the Saudi Crown Prince holds talks in Cairo. 
Lorenzo Kamel, professor of international history at the University of Turin, told Al Jazeera that Ansar Allah operates with growing local autonomy and is not merely an Iranian proxy, but is capitalising on regional chaos to force concessions from Riyadh. He said Saudi Arabia has historically outsourced its security to the United States, which "will never bring a formal lasting peace". On Washington's hesitation to intervene directly in Yemen, Kamel said the US has "paid a harsh price in recent months" and is wary of the midterm elections, accusing Iran of "weaponising the markets" to create an economic shockwave before the vote. He said Iran cannot fully close the Strait of Hormuz while the US cannot fully open it, meaning the stalemate is likely to continue, and warned that Tehran has an interest in choosing escalation over surrender.

recentItems.title: Gaza building collapse leaves at least 11 dead and more than 100 trapped
recentItems.description:
A residential building in Gaza City has collapsed, leaving at least 70 people missing, including children. Rescuers have pulled out 11 bodies and 12 survivors, while Gaza Civil Defence says more than 100 Palestinians are still trapped beneath the rubble, including at least 50 children. The building, which housed displaced people, had previously been damaged in an Israeli strike, leaving it cracked and structurally unsound. Families had no other choice but to shelter inside the partially damaged structure, which collapsed as they were sleeping at around 1am. Rescue crews and residents have been digging through the rubble, with a lack of heavy equipment making rescue operations more difficult. Civil Defence says at least 2,000 buildings in Gaza are in a similar condition and at risk of collapse at any moment. There is a severe shortage of shelter, with people forced to live in partially damaged buildings because of a lack of tents and other shelter supplies. Israel continues to restrict the entry of construction materials and equipment into Gaza, while promised shelter supplies under the ceasefire have yet to materialise on the ground. 

Al Jazeera's Hind Khoudary reports from Gaza City.
